content: "Instead of disposing of garden prunings by burning or shredding them this winter, consider creating a dead hedge. This eco-friendly structure serves as an excellent windbreak, provides a sanctuary for local wildlife, and can effectively separate different sections of your garden. Start by hammering stakes or repurposing old fence posts into the ground, arranging them in parallel lines about 50cm apart. Begin filling this framework by inserting your pruned materials, placing the thicker branches at the bottom. Over time, the structure will naturally compact as you continue to add more. In another refreshing idea, if your holiday gifts left you underwhelmed, brighten your spirits by pre-ordering 'The Book Of Seeds' by Paul Smith ($30, Ivy Press), due to be released in February. This beautifully detailed book explores 600 bizarre and stunning plant seeds worldwide. Additionally, consider planting a winter-blooming clematis. Species like Clematis cirrhosa ‘Advent Bells’ and ‘Jingle Bells’ offer vibrant blooms through the winter months and thrive in sunny, sheltered locations, adding color and life to your garden during the colder seasons."
